newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish crown slips and the yield curve flattens.
newsitem.headline: Swedish crown slips and the yield curve flattens.

text.p: 1415 GMT - The Swedish crown lost ground substantially against both the mark and the dollar on Thursday and the yield curve flattened.
Dealers said London based banks were selling crowns.
* Six month T-bill rate flat at 4.34 pct
* 10-year bond yield down one basis point to 6.59 pct
* Mark firms to 4.3615 against the crown from 4.3425
* Dollar firms to 8.0445 from 7.9790 late on Wednesday
The Swedish crown weakened considerably on Thursday and the Swedish yield curve continued to flatten amid speculations of a German rate hike.
Heavy selling from London based banks triggered the crown's fall, dealers said.
The spread between Swedish and German long yields increased three basis points to 91.
"The crown has lost substantially index-wise. We have a range for the spread to Germany of 85-100 basis points. I could well imagine the spread to go up to 100," one dealer said.
She said it depended on how the crown performed.
"I think many foreigners are long. If they start selling the spread could continue up," she said.
Ten-year bond yields decreased one basis point to 6.59 percent and six-month T-bill rates ended flat at 4.34 percent.
The mark firmed to 4.3615 against the crown from 4.3425 on Wednesday and the dollar changed hands almost seven ore higher at 8.0445 compared to 7.9790.
